 research doc (still outside git), as one table with every figure labelled MEASURED, ASSUMED or OPEN. I also added the stock firmware's footprint on the chip to §10's open unknowns. I checked the table's columns and re-ran all the arithmetic in a script.

- **Why QMK takes nothing:** in the SonixQMK source (`sn32_develop` branch), QMK's program runs from the keyboard chip's own 256 KB of internal flash. Its settings storage (keymap, VIA) defaults to internal flash too. The only reservation on the 16 MB chip is 8 KB for the gallery's own index.
- **Only one number is measured:** the 30,720-byte frame size, from our own captures and the real screen. The 16 MB capacity comes from a teardown of this model, not our unit, so it's labelled ASSUMED.
- **What limits the gallery:** the stock firmware's data on the chip. If we hold an off-board copy of the chip, it can be overwritten and all 511 slots are usable. If we don't, the count is 511 minus whatever stock keeps there. I haven't guessed that size. If the stock firmware's backup partitions live on this chip, overwriting them would also destroy a way back to stock.
- **How to measure it:** copy the chip's full contents and count the sectors that aren't blank. That means either a clip on the chip, which requires opening the case (irreversible), or a read-only copy from a QMK build on the spare board before anything is written to the chip.
- **Porting catches found in the source:** QMK's flash driver defaults to a 512 KB chip, so a port that doesn't set 16 MB would only ever use the first 32nd of it. And QMK's image loader expects images in memory the chip can read directly, which the 16 MB chip isn't, so a gallery needs a bit of custom read-and-display code.
- **Images built into the firmware instead:** at most 8 frames would fit in internal flash, even if QMK took no space. That's why a gallery has to live on the external chip.

Nothing else can move without the keyboard, so I'm going back to idle.
